extracted.intended_audience: Stakeholders in the U.S. patent system (inventors, patent owners, investors, licensees, accused infringers and their counsel, patent practitioners, companies, academic and research institutions, IP organizations, nonprofits, government agencies)
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO public comment on patent eligibility
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and specific question set for written public comments to the USPTO study on the current state of patent subject-matter eligibility jurisprudence in the United States, soliciting experiences, impacts, examples, and data from stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify yourself and your interest in the U.S. patent system
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding to the questions, please identify yourself and your interest in the U.S. patent system. If applicable, indicate whether you fall within one or more of the following categories: (1) inventors, patent owners, or investors (e.g., venture capital, investment bank, fund, etc.); (2) licensees or users of patented technology; (3) entities that represent inventors or patent owners (e.g., law firms); (4) recipients of demand letters concerning alleged patent infringement or accused infringers in a patent lawsuit; (5) entities that represent accused infringers; (6) government agencies or officials; (7) academic or non-profit institutions; (8) intellectual property organizations or associations; and (9) nonprofit organizations or advocacy groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, if you are a patent owner or inventor, please include the number of U.S. and foreign patent applications you have filed; the number of U.S. and foreign patents you hold; the number of patents you have licensed or sold; and the number of patent cases you have been involved in since the Supreme Court's decision in Bilski (2010).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1 – Effects on business conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain how the current state of patent eligibility jurisprudence affects the conduct of business in your technology area(s). Please identify the technology area(s) in your response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific technology areas and describe business conduct changes (e.g., strategy, planning) attributable to current jurisprudence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 – Specific impacts across business activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain what impacts, if any, you have experienced as a result of the current state of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States. Please include impacts on as many of the following areas as you can, identifying concrete examples and supporting facts when possible:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas listed: (a) Patent prosecution strategy and portfolio management; (b) patent enforcement and litigation; (c) patent counseling and opinion work; (d) research and development; (e) employment; (f) procurement; (g) marketing; (h) ability to obtain funding from investors or financial institutions; (i) investment strategy; (j) licensing of patents and patent applications; (k) product development; (l) sales, including downstream and upstream sales; (m) innovation; (n) competition. Provide concrete examples and supporting facts when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 – Impacts on particular technological fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain how the current state of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States impacts particular technological fields, including investment and innovation in any of the following technological areas:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields listed: (a) Quantum computing; (b) artificial intelligence; (c) precision medicine; (d) diagnostic methods; (e) pharmaceutical treatments; and (f) other computer-related inventions (e.g., software, business methods, computer security, databases and data structures, computer networking, and graphical user interfaces). In responding, please provide concrete examples and supporting facts when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4 – Comparative experiences in other jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain how your experiences with the application of subject-matter eligibility requirements in other jurisdictions, including China, Japan, Korea, and Europe, differ from your experiences in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific procedural or substantive differences and practical effects on prosecution, enforcement, commercialization, or investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5 – Instances of differing outcomes between U.S. and foreign jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please identify instances where you have been denied patent protection for an invention in the United States solely on the basis of subject-matter ineligibility but obtained protection for the same invention in a foreign jurisdiction, or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific examples (technology and jurisdiction involved) and the reason the invention was held ineligible in the United States or other jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6 – Shifts in investment, R&D, or jobs across jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain whether the state of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States has caused you to modify or shift investment, research and development activities, or jobs from the United States to other jurisdictions, or to the United States from other jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If so, identify the relevant modifications and their associated impacts (e.g., where activity moved, scale of change, rationale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7 – Changes in business strategies for IP protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain whether the state of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States has caused you to change business strategies for protecting your intellectual property (e.g., shifting from patents to trade secrets, or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If so, identify the changes and their associated impacts (e.g., operational, competitive, financial consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 – Changes in filing/purchasing/licensing/maintaining behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain whether you have changed your behavior with regard to filing, purchasing, licensing, selling, or maintaining patent applications and patents in the United States as a result of the current state of patent eligibility jurisprudence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If so, describe how you changed your behavior and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9 – Effects on patent litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain how, in your experience, the status of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States has affected any litigation for patent infringement in the United States in which you have been involved as a party, as legal counsel, or as another participant (e.g., an expert witness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, explain whether this jurisprudence has affected the cost or duration of such litigation, the ability to defend against claims of patent infringement, the certainty/uncertainty of litigation outcomes, or the likelihood of settlement. Provide concrete examples and supporting facts when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10 – Impact on global strength of U.S. intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Please identify how the current state of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States impacts the global strength of U.S. intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss effects on international competitiveness, enforcement, and perceived value of U.S. IP rights, with concrete examples if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11 – Impact on the U.S. economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please identify how the current state of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States impacts the U.S. economy as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss macroeconomic effects such as investment, jobs, innovation, and sectoral impacts, providing data or examples where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 12 – Economic/market impacts in listed technological areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Please identify how the current state of subject matter eligibility jurisprudence in the United States impacts the global strength of U.S. intellectual property and the U.S. economy in any of the following areas:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas listed: (a) Quantum computing; (b) artificial intelligence; (c) precision medicine; (d) diagnostic methods; (e) pharmaceutical treatments; and (f) other computer-related inventions (e.g., software, business methods, computer security, databases and data structures, computer networking, and graphical user interfaces). Provide concrete examples and supporting facts when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 13 – Effects on the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Please identify how the current state of patent eligibility jurisprudence in the United States affects the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, discuss whether the jurisprudence affects, either positively or negatively, the availability, effectiveness, or cost of personalized medicine, diagnostics, pharmaceutical treatments, software, or computer-implemented inventions. Provide concrete examples and supporting facts when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition questions presented to the Supreme Court (as background)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitions presented the questions: (1) What is the appropriate standard for determining whether a claim is directed to a patent-ineligible concept under step one of the Alice two-step framework? and (2) Is patent eligibility a question of law for the court or a question of fact for the jury?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These background legal questions frame the study; comments addressing standards for 'directed to' analyses or the law/fact allocation are responsive. Cite case examples or concrete litigation/prosecution effects if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission logistics, format, and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted through the Federal eRulemaking Portal (www.regulations.gov) to docket PTO-P-2021-0032 by the stated deadline (extended to October 15, 2021). Electronic submissions in Adobe portable document format (PDF) or Microsoft Word are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure/proprietary business information should be clearly identified if submitted; accepted submissions will be made available for public inspection unless designated. If electronic submission is not feasible, contact the USPTO for special instructions. Commenters need not respond to every question and may provide relevant information even if not responsive to a particular question.
